A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIPFUSION research and provide readable methods, equations, experiments, and appendices. Existing content can be matched despite pagination changes and appendix additions in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original CLIPFUSION classification and segmentation results on MVTec-AD and VisA, including ablations and one-for-all experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds results for alternative state descriptors, fusion weights, and diffusion backbones.

M1.justification: PatchCLIP and MapDiff feature extraction, empty-mask diffusion inputs, memory-bank comparisons, and fusion/scoring procedures are unchanged. Appendix A.9 restates the existing method as pseudocode; alternative backbones are evaluated as configurations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MVTec-AD and VisA anomaly classification and segmentation under zero-shot, few-shot, and one-for-all settings. The added analyses and failure examples remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: Trans-MM, MaskCLIP, CLIP-AC, PaDiM, PatchCore, WinCLIP, PromptAD, and IIPAD retain their membership in the corresponding comparisons. MuSc's revised discussion does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluations with two alternative state-descriptor sets in Table 12 and Stable Diffusion v1.5/v2.1 backbones in Table 16. The fusion-weight grid was already specified in v2 Appendix A.2; retained experimental protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds focused descriptor-set and backbone robustness tests and two failure case studies. Table 15 provides fuller numerical evidence for the previously described weight sweep. These extend the retained component, extraction, and training-sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify means and standard deviations over five differently seeded runs and retain Figure 4's seed-sensitivity analysis. New appendix tables follow the existing ablation tables' point-estimate reporting style.

E6.justification: Primary and matched per-category results are unchanged. Tables 12, 15, and 16 add result entries; for example, Table 16 reports MVTec-AD classification scores of 93.5 with Stable Diffusion v1.5 and 94.6 with v2.1, alongside 95.4 with v2.0. These compare different backbone configurations.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 and the probabilistic interpretation of cross-attention averaging are unchanged. The new pseudocode repeats existing calculations without adding mathematical assumptions, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the claims about complementary CLIP/diffusion features, task coverage, performance, and efficiency. Replacing 'entirely training-free' with 'no additional training' clarifies the already-described use of pretrained models.

C2.justification: Appendix A.7 adds specific failure explanations: repetitive cable wires distract diffusion attention, while the missing-transistor example exposes insufficient contextual understanding. v3 also interprets the added descriptor and backbone comparisons as robustness evidence.

D1.justification: Section 6.4 newly clarifies that the one-for-all comparison otherwise follows Section 5's experimental settings. Appendix A.9 consolidates the existing procedure into pseudocode for both tasks. Core preprocessing, hardware, and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works are unchanged. Section 2 replaces the statement that MuSc requires the entire test set and a low anomaly proportion with a batch-processing requirement. The introduction also explicitly positions CLIPFUSION as using off-the-shelf models without retraining or a shared module.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order are retained. v3 adds brief cross-attention and few-shot explanations, appendix subsections A.6–A.9, pseudocode, and acknowledgments, and refines the training-free terminology.

P2.justification: v3 adds three result tables, a two-panel failure figure, and two algorithm displays. Existing figures, tables, and qualitative galleries are retained with relocation or renumbering. Publication headers and adjusted table placement also change the layout.

improvement.justification: Tables 12, 15, and 16 make robustness and weight-selection evidence more assessable than in v2. The explicit failure cases and pseudocode improve transparency and usability. These are useful, limited gains while the core method and primary empirical evidence remain unchanged.
